title: DBM releases P336M for hog raisers affected by ASF
summary: The Department of Budget and Management (DBM) has released P336 million to fund the compensation of hog raisers affected by African swine fever (ASF).

blocks.text: The Department of Budget and Management (DBM) has released P336 million to fund the compensation of hog raisers affected by African swine fever (ASF).

During the interpellation of the Department of Agriculture's (DA) budget at the Senate plenary, Senator Risa Hontiveros raised that more than 8,400 hog raisers and traders affected by ASF from 2023 to 2026 have yet to be paid by the government for their losses. They are owed a total of P434 million.

Senator Francis Pangilinan, the DA's budget sponsor in the Senate, said the DBM had not released the contingency fund. However, Pangilinan was informed on the spot that DBM released the fund on Thursday night. He quipped that perhaps the agency knew that Hontiveros was about to ask that question.
"So P336 million has been released, unpaid is P229 million as of 2024, and December, the payout will start," Pangilinan said.
The remaining balance will be sourced from quick response funds, Pangilinan said. The balance will be fully paid by the end of the first quarter of 2027.
"Just for the record, your Committee on Agriculture has been following this up since July. And after five months, it has been released," said Pangilinan in a mix of English and Filipino.
ASF first hit the Philippines in 2019, severely affecting the country's hog industry and reducing its swine population from around 13 million heads to about 8 million.
The Bureau of Animal Industry has reported ASF outbreaks in 76 of the country's 82 provinces. — VDV, GMA News
